_comment: 14 hand-compiled K-IR v0.1 atoms covering every 'nastiest case' named: Copper/Metal/Material specialization chain (+ the 2 ontology facts needed to make it actually derivable, not just asserted), Metal/Semiconductor apparent contradiction, water 0-4C apparent contradiction, Dropout train/inference apparent contradiction, DropConnect/Dropout generalization, and the BatchNorm genuine contradiction. See STRESS_TEST.md for what broke while compiling these.

surface_forms: Ordinary solids expand when heated, at constant pressure.
atoms.notes: modality=generic because negative-thermal-expansion materials (e.g. some zirconium tungstates) are real named exceptions.

surface_forms: Metals expand when heated.
atoms.notes: modality=generic because Invar-type low-expansion alloys are a real named exception. Identical predicate/arguments/direction/context to KIR-001, differing ONLY in quantification.type -- see STRESS_TEST.md finding 1 (the positive result).

surface_forms: Copper expands when heated.
A copper rod gets longer as its temperature increases.
atoms.notes: modality=universal (no known exception for solid copper below melting). Identical predicate/arguments/direction/context to KIR-002 except quantification.type AND modality -- the modality difference is exactly why naive subtype-based entailment derivation is unsound here. See STRESS_TEST.md finding 1.

surface_forms: Copper is a metal.
Metal is a material.
For most ordinary metals, electrical resistance increases as temperature increases.
atoms.notes: modality=generic: special low-TCR alloys are real named exceptions.

surface_forms: For intrinsic silicon, resistance decreases as temperature increases.
No material is both a metal and a semiconductor.
atoms.notes: Benchmark-level simplification, not physical truth -- real metallic/semiconducting behavior is a transport regime that can depend on doping/pressure/phase, not an eternal class property. Same caveat as the physics/ML benchmarks' scope_notes.

surface_forms: For a fixed mass of liquid water, volume increases with temperature above 4C.
atoms.notes: STRESS TEST: value_domain.max = 'boiling_point(x)' is a bare STRING, not a structured function term -- the schema's ValueDomainConstraint.max only accepts number|string|null, not a Term reference. This loses the fact that the bound is itself a function of x. See STRESS_TEST.md finding 5.

surface_forms: Between 0C and 4C, water contracts as it warms.
During training, dropout randomly zeroes unit activations.
atoms.notes: STRESS TEST: M041's full claim is a conjunction (masks activations AND prevents co-adaptation AND acts as implicit ensemble). This atom captures only the mechanistic core; the two causal/effect claims have no home in a single-predicate atom. See STRESS_TEST.md finding 2.

surface_forms: At inference, dropout masking is disabled.
atoms.notes: Corrected per review: only asserts masking is off. Inverted dropout's compensatory activation scaling happened during training (KIR-010's phase), not restated here. KIR-010 and KIR-011 are identical except phase (context) and polarity (assert vs negate) -- clean, structural, exactly what the flagship context-preservation pair should look like.

surface_forms: DropConnect randomly zeroes individual connection weights during training.
atoms.notes: STRESS TEST: DropConnect GENERALIZES Dropout (zeroing all weights out of one unit = zeroing that unit's activation) but this is a relationship between the DEFINITIONS of Weight(w)-aggregated-over-a-unit and Activation(u), which this schema has no way to state. Without a Definition/derivation construct connecting the two function symbols, the GENERALIZES relation between KIR-012 and KIR-010 is not structurally derivable -- it can only be asserted by a human/LLM as a pairwise judgment, exactly the P02 problem recurring at the representation level. See STRESS_TEST.md finding 3.

surface_forms: Batch normalization improves training primarily by reducing internal covariate shift.
atoms.notes: STRESS TEST: forced into HOLDS(PrimaryMechanism(BatchNorm), <bare constant string>). There is no principled predicate for 'X's primary explanatory mechanism is Y' in this vocabulary. See STRESS_TEST.md finding 4.

surface_forms: Batch normalization's main benefit is smoothing the optimization landscape, not reducing internal covariate shift.
atoms.notes: Deliberately SAME (empty) context as KIR-013 -- genuine contradiction, not an apparent one. POSITIVE FINDING: if PrimaryMechanism is declared FUNCTIONAL (single-valued) as predicate-signature metadata, CONTRADICTS between KIR-013 and KIR-014 becomes MECHANICALLY DERIVABLE (two HOLDS atoms assigning different values to the same functional role under identical context = contradiction by construction), rather than a hand-labeled pair judgment. This schema has no 'functional argument' metadata yet -- see STRESS_TEST.md finding 4.

surface_forms: Every square is a rectangle.
atoms.notes: CONTROL CASE: deliberately easy, same shape as KIR-004/KIR-007. Schema handles this cleanly -- included to show the breaks below are real gaps, not the schema being broken everywhere.

surface_forms: Every differentiable function is continuous.
atoms.notes: STRESS TEST (severe, new): predicate 'IMPLIES' does not exist in the original 6-predicate vocabulary and is needed the moment ANY general logical implication between two properties appears -- not physics-specific. Worse: Differentiable(f) and Continuous(f) are being used as Term.function values, but they are actually BOOLEAN PROPOSITIONS, not value-returning terms -- this is an abuse of the Term grammar. v0.1 has no first-class 'proposition as argument' construct. See STRESS_TEST.md finding 6. The converse (every continuous function is differentiable) is FALSE -- this pair is the cleanest possible test of whether canonicalization respects entailment direction rather than treating shared predicates as identity.

surface_forms: Hash-table lookup is expected O(1) under suitable hashing assumptions.
atoms.notes: STRESS TEST (new dimension): 'measure=expected' is smuggled into the free-text assumptions list, but this is NOT a world-condition like phase or regime -- it's which STATISTIC of a random runtime is being reported (expected vs worst-case vs amortized). Conflating 'aggregation/measure type' with 'background assumption' means nothing structurally distinguishes this from KIR-018. See STRESS_TEST.md finding 7.

surface_forms: Hash-table lookup is O(1).
atoms.notes: Decoy: unqualified. True if read as the same implicit expected-case claim as KIR-017; false if read as worst-case (degenerate collisions give O(n)). The English is genuinely AMBIGUOUS about which reading is meant -- compiling this at all requires the LLM frontend to guess/resolve an ambiguity the source text never resolved. K-IR can expose that ambiguity (e.g. flag measure=unspecified) but cannot fix it.

surface_forms: A serializable schedule behaves as some serial execution.
atoms.notes: STRESS TEST (new predicate, brand new category): needed a wholly new predicate, OBSERVATIONALLY_EQUIVALENT_TO -- outcome-equivalence between a concurrent execution and SOME serial ordering, which is definitionally NOT the same as literal sequential execution (KIR-020). Nothing in MONOTONIC/EQUALS/SUBTYPE_OF/etc. is remotely this shape. See STRESS_TEST.md finding 8.

surface_forms: A serializable schedule runs transactions one at a time.
atoms.notes: FALSE as a general property -- serializability guarantees observational equivalence (KIR-019) to SOME serial order, never that execution is literally sequential (real systems interleave for performance). Included specifically to test whether near-identical surface wording ('behaves as serial' vs 'runs serially') gets wrongly canonicalized to the SAME predicate. Correct relation to KIR-019: UNRELATED predicates (not EQUAL, not strictly CONTRADICTS either -- see STRESS_TEST.md finding 9 on why 'CONTRADICTS' is the wrong label for a true-property-vs-false-property pair).

surface_forms: If X and Y are independent, Cov(X,Y)=0 (given finite second moments).
atoms.notes: STRESS TEST (single worst break found): 'CovarianceIsZero(X,Y)' is a MADE-UP function name standing in for the full proposition 'Covariance(X,Y) = 0', because v0.1 cannot nest a real EQUALS proposition as the consequent of an IMPLIES proposition -- there is no recursive Proposition-as-Term support at all. Any real implementation needs this. The converse (Cov=0 implies independence) is FALSE in general -- another clean directional-entailment test, layered on top of the nesting problem. See STRESS_TEST.md finding 6 (same root cause as KIR-016).

surface_forms: TCP provides an ordered byte stream.
atoms.notes: STRESS TEST (contrast with KIR-013/014): Guarantees(TCP) looks like the same 'HOLDS(FunctionalRole(subject), value)' shape as PrimaryMechanism(BatchNorm), but it is NOT single-valued -- a protocol guarantees MANY properties simultaneously (ordering, byte-stream semantics, congestion control...). The 'declare functional -> auto-derive CONTRADICTS' trick from KIR-013/014 does NOT generalize here: two different HOLDS(Guarantees(TCP), P) atoms with different P are NOT automatically contradictory. v0.1 has no way to mark a role SET-VALUED vs FUNCTIONAL. See STRESS_TEST.md finding 10.

surface_forms: TCP preserves application message boundaries.
atoms.notes: FALSE -- TCP is a byte stream; message framing is an application-layer or SCTP-layer concern. Included to test high-lexical-similarity/low-semantic-relation (shares 'Guarantees(TCP)' subject with KIR-022, near-identical topic, unrelated actual property). ALSO exposes a second gap: provenance.confidence has no value for 'flatly false / refuted common belief' -- 'contested' and 'superseded' both wrongly imply it was ever a majority accepted view. See STRESS_TEST.md finding 11.

surface_forms: No massive object locally accelerates through the speed of light.

provenance.source: FLRW cosmology / metric expansion of space

surface_forms: Distant galaxies can recede faster than light due to cosmic expansion.
atoms.notes: STRESS TEST (deepest finding): KIR-024A and KIR-024B use DIFFERENT function symbols (LocalPeculiarVelocity vs CosmologicalRecessionRate) for what natural language calls 'velocity' in both. This is NOT a context-disambiguation problem solvable by adding a context field to one shared Velocity(x) symbol the way water/dropout/attention were -- it requires SYMBOL RESOLUTION (picking the right formal quantity) at compile time, before context-matching is even relevant. A compiler that naively mapped both onto one shared symbol and tried to reconcile via context would either invent a fake regime split with no physical referent, or fail to unify them and miss that these are genuinely COMPATIBLE. See STRESS_TEST.md finding 12 -- arguably the single most important finding in this batch, because it shows the context-reconciliation strategy that worked for every earlier 'apparent contradiction' case has a real scope limit.
